title: Senior's toolkit: programs and APIs
summary: Calling programs and HTTP APIs from scripts that run unattended: the switches that make them fail loudly, quickly and safely.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: programs and APIs
steps.body: Most automation glues programs and APIs together. These commands, with these switches, are what makes the glue hold at 3 a.m.

toolkit.what: The exit code of the last native program. Check it after every program that matters.
flags: pass a program's code on to your caller
toolkit.example:
git push origin main
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "git push failed ($LASTEXITCODE)" }

toolkit.what: PowerShell 7.4+: a non-zero exit code becomes a PowerShell error, so 'Stop' stops.
flags: turn it on for the script
needed too, to make it terminating

toolkit.what: Run a program whose path has spaces or is in a variable.
flags: stop parsing: pass the rest verbatim (Windows legacy tools)

toolkit.what: Installers, elevation, GUI apps, other users.
Call a REST API; JSON comes back as objects.
The raw response: status, headers, content, downloads.
Read every page of a paginated API.
flags: guard against a server that never ends

steps.prompt: Match the failure to the switch that prevents it.
pairs: The job hung for 8 hours on one call
A deploy-time 503 failed the nightly report
The report counted only the first 100 users
`git push` failed and the script said done
A 404 should be a warning, not a crash

steps.prompt: `robocopy D:\data \\nas\backup /MIR` finishes and `$LASTEXITCODE` is 3. What does that mean?
options: Success: files were copied and extra files found (robocopy codes 0-7 are success)
steps.explain: Robocopy's exit code is a bit field: 1 = files copied, 2 = extra files, 4 = mismatches; 8 and above means at least one failure. A wrapper should treat `$LASTEXITCODE -ge 8` as failure.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: After every program call that matters, check `$LASTEXITCODE` against the program's documented codes. Give every HTTP call a timeout, retries when the call is idempotent, and a pagination loop when the answer is a list. Never put a token in the script; read it from a secret store.
